text:
Anna: Quick sync — we need a concise drain plan for trace-ingest when we scale-down pods. Yesterday's scale-in leaked partial batches and messed up span attribution. Anyone seen similar?
Jordan: saw it — ~0.6% of spans dropped during a surprise scale-in in prod :grimacing:. Happens when SIGTERM closes connections before kv-cache flush.
Sam: can you paste the shutdown logs you saw? curious how the worker loop behaved.
Anna: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-16T18:12:03Z INFO received SIGTERM, entering DRAINING
2026-03-16T18:12:03Z INFO stop-accepting new connections
2026-03-16T18:12:07Z WARN flush timeout reached, terminating process
```
Mike: that 4s flush timeout is the killer for large tenants. We need drain semantics that minimize data loss but bound tail latency / cost.
Anna: proposal sketch: (1) set pod state -> DRAINING in router metadata, (2) router stops routing new envelopes to pod, (3) pod finishes current batches up to a configurable grace period, (4) if unfinished, requeue remaining envelopes with a `drain_marker` header, (5) sinks make dedupe decisions on `idempotency_key` + `drain_marker`.
Jordan: tradeoffs: requeue gives us safety but increases duplicate-handling work downstream and can temporarily spike load/cost. If we requeue naively we risk double-billing for attributed traces.
Sam: how about per-envelope sequence + per-tenant dedupe TTL? e.g., attach `seq=(tenant,seq)` and the sink drops duplicates seen within TTL. TTL stores are expensive though.
Mike: alternative: use partition-level drain offsets. When a pod drains, it writes its last-offset marker to the partition metadata. Consumers detect overlap windows and drop already-processed offsets cheaply (no global dedupe store). Cheaper, but requires tight contract with consumer offsets.
Anna: agree partition-offset approach is promising. Also we should add `drain_origin=pod_id` and `drain_offset` to requeued envelopes to help consumers decide. Config example:
```yaml
ingest:
  shutdown_grace: 15s
  drain_requeue: true
  drain_marker_ttl: 1h
```
Sam: metric/obs checklist: gauge `ingest_inflight_batches{pod}`, counter `drain_requeues_total`, hist `drain_flush_duration_seconds`. Also emit an event when drain exceeds grace.
Jordan: SLO considerations: we should aim for <0.1% span-loss on controlled scale-ins for 95th percentile tenants. Uncontrolled (surprise) scale-ins get best-effort.
Mike: implementation tasks: router API to set pod state + small metadata store change for `last_committed_offset` write on drain. Consumer change to ignore overlapping offsets (idempotent commit). Also add e2e tests simulating race between commit & requeue.
Anna: security/consistency note: requeued envelopes should preserve original auth/tenant headers, and `drain_marker` must not be user-controllable.
Sam: I'll own a spike: build a harness that simulates concurrent ingest, a scale-in, and validate no loss for >99.9% under load. Will test both requeue and partition-marker approaches.
Jordan: please also measure cost delta (extra CPU / storage) for the requeue flow. We need numbers before deciding default grace.
CICD Bot: FYI: when this lands, run a canary rollout where only scale-ins on 10% of pods follow new drain logic for 72h.
Anna: Great. I'll draft an RFC capturing both approaches (requeue vs partition-marker) and the metrics/SLOs. Sam will attach the spike results. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Sam: I'll post the spike results in this thread in ~48h.
Mike: small ask — add a tiny config to override `shutdown_grace` per-tenant for high-volume customers. We can set 30s temporarily for some big tenants.
Anna: noted. I'll include a per-tenant override section in the RFC.
